title: Hash map pair search
watch: Before index right is inserted, the map holds only values at indexes smaller than right. The answer appears when target - value is already a key.

title: Two pointers on a sorted array
watch: Every pair outside [left, right] has been ruled out: a total below target moves left up, a total above target moves right down.

title: Monotonic stack: next greater value
watch: The stack holds indexes still waiting for a greater value; their values never increase from bottom to top. Each index is pushed once and popped at most once.

title: Binary search: first index with nums[i] ≥ target
watch: The answer always stays in [lo, hi]. Everything left of lo is below target; everything from hi on is at least target. Each step halves the range.

title: One-dimensional DP: best subarray ending here
watch: running is the best sum of a subarray that ends at x; best is the best sum seen anywhere so far. A negative running sum is dropped by restarting at x.

title: Reversing a linked list in place
watch: previous is the already-reversed part and head is the rest. One assignment turns head's link around and advances both pointers, so no node is lost.

title: Breadth-first search frontier
watch: The queue holds the frontier in order of distance. A node gets its distance the first time it is discovered, and that distance is final.

title: Merge sort: split, recurse, merge
watch: Each call sorts its own slice. While merging, out holds the smallest items of left and right in order; ties take the left item first, which keeps the sort stable.

title: Sliding window without repeats
watch: text[left:right + 1] never contains a repeated character. When character was seen inside the window, left jumps just past its last position; it never moves back.

driver: inorder_iterative([4, [2, [1, None, None], [3, None, None]], [6, [5, None, None], None]])
title: In-order traversal with an explicit stack
watch: The stack holds the ancestors whose left subtree is being visited. A node is output after its whole left subtree and before its right one.

title: Min-heap of the k largest
watch: The heap never holds more than k values and its root is the smallest of them. A new value that beats the root survives; the root is dropped.

title: Topological order by in-degree (Kahn)
watch: A task enters ready only when every task it depends on is already in order. If tasks remain but ready is empty, the graph has a cycle.

title: Dijkstra with a priority queue
watch: With nonnegative weights, the smallest cost popped for u is final. Older, larger entries for u are skipped. Each relaxation lowers dist[v] and pushes the new cost.

title: Two-dimensional DP: longest common subsequence
watch: dp[i][j] is the LCS length of a[:i] and b[:j]. It extends dp[i-1][j-1] on a match, and otherwise takes the better of dropping one character.

driver:
d = DSU(6)
for a, b in [(0, 1), (2, 3), (1, 3), (4, 5)]:
    d.union(a, b)
result = [d.find(x) for x in range(6)]
title: Union–find: union by size with path halving
watch: Each set is a tree and its root is the representative. Union hangs the smaller tree under the larger root; find shortens the path as it climbs.
